battle.name: 第一次塔臘納基戰爭
battle.theater: 塔臘納基惠塔拉與新普利茅斯
battle.brief: 一八六〇年三月，紐西蘭北島塔臘納基，總督布朗不顧毛利首領反對仍買下六百英畝土地，兩軍在 Te Kohia 與 Waireka 交火，一八六一年三月停火。卡面加特林機槍同年才在美國做出原型，兩年後才取得專利；塔臘納基真正壓制塹壕的仍是臼砲、火箭與恩菲爾德步槍。

kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰雙方，是英國本土與其紐西蘭殖民地政府一方，以及以 Te Āti Awa 為核心、由毛利王運動在背後支撐的塔臘納基毛利聯軍一方。英方由總督湯瑪斯·戈爾·布朗掌舵，殖民部與議會在背後批准撥款與調兵；帝國正規軍方面，第 65 步兵團自一八五九年駐紮紐西蘭，隨後有第 40 步兵團由奧克蘭調來，另有皇家陸軍砲兵隊與皇家海軍分遣隊登岸作戰，輔以一八五八年成立的塔臘納基民兵與一八五九年成立的塔臘納基來福鎗志願隊，總計從澳洲與英國本土運來的帝國部隊約三千五百人。毛利方的編制沒有常設指揮系統，靠各部族依毛利協商規矩聯合：Te Āti Awa 出面主張土地權，Ngāti Maniapoto、Ngāti Ruanui、Ngāti Rauru、Ngāti Hauā 等部族以戰隊形式參與，武器與彈藥則靠奧克蘭、懷烏庫與卡菲亞一帶的黑市供應；站在他們背後的是毛利王運動，國王波塔圖·特·韋羅韋羅是名義上的領袖，維雷米·塔米哈納與埃皮哈·托科希希是實際的推動者。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the British state together with the Colony of New Zealand on one hand, and on the other a Taranaki Maori coalition centred on Te Atiawa and politically backed by the Maori King Movement. The British side was run by Governor Thomas Gore Browne, with the Colonial Office and the colonial legislature approving money and reinforcements behind him; on the imperial regular side the 65th Regiment of Foot had been stationed in New Zealand since 1859, the 40th Regiment was brought down from Auckland, and there were the Royal Artillery, a naval brigade landed from the Royal Navy, the Taranaki Militia formed in 1858 and the Taranaki Rifle Volunteers formed in 1859; imperial troops brought from Australia and from Britain itself numbered about 3,500. The Maori side had no standing command system and relied on the various iwi joining under tikanga: Te Atiawa put forward the claim to the land, while Ngati Maniapoto, Ngati Ruanui, Ngati Rauru, Ngati Haua and others joined as war parties, their weapons and ammunition bought on the black market around Auckland, Waiuku and Kawhia; behind them stood the Maori King Movement, with King Potatau Te Wherowhero as its figurehead and Wiremu Tamihana and Epiha Tokohihi as the men who actually drove it.
people: 推動這場戰爭的是文官而不是將軍。總督布朗是整件事的關鍵：他在明知 Wiremu Kīngi 反對的情況下仍接受 Te Teira 的土地買賣，宣布全區戒嚴，簽下土地契據，並在連敗之後召開奧克蘭科希馬拉馬會議，試圖用條約把事情收場。英軍前後有兩任指揮官：第 65 團中校查爾斯·埃米利烏斯·戈爾德負責佔領惠塔拉，三月十七日下令向 Te Kohia 的 pā 開火，戰爭由此爆開，六月二十七日 Puketakauere 慘敗後被撤換；少將湯瑪斯·西姆森·普拉特接任，改用慢速的工兵掘進，一八六一年一月攻擊惠朗基，最後促成三月十八日停火。底下還有少校湯瑪斯·納爾遜（率三百五十人攻 Puketakauere）、上尉威廉·梅西傑（夜行沼澤遭伏的分隊長）、上尉鮑德勒、中校喬治·弗里曼·默里（Waireka 撤退遭譴責）、HMS Niger 艦長彼得·克拉克羅夫特（水兵夜襲奪旗）、海軍分遣隊指揮官博尚普·西摩，以及率武裝定居者死守 Jury 農莊的查爾斯·布朗上尉。毛利一方，Wiremu Kīngi 是維權派首領，Te Whiti 北上尋求仲裁，Hapurona 是 Te Āti Awa 的戰將兼 Puketakauere 的佈陣者，Rewi Maniapoto 率隊夜襲三號碉堡，維雷米·塔米哈納在中間斡旋停火，Te Rei Hanataua 則在 Waireka 陣亡。HMS Niger 的一等水兵威廉·奧傑斯因奪下毛利旗幟獲頒維多利亞十字勳章，是新西蘭戰爭史上第一枚。
peopleEn: What drove this war was a civil servant rather than a general. Governor Browne was the pivot: he took the purchase from Te Teira knowing full well that Wiremu Kingi opposed it, proclaimed martial law over the district, signed the deed, and after the successive defeats tried to close the matter with a conference at Kohimarama in Auckland. The British force had two commanders in turn. Lieutenant Colonel Charles Emilius Gold of the 65th Regiment was ordered to occupy Waitara, opened fire on the Te Kohia pa on 17 March and thereby started the war, and after the disaster at Puketakauere on 27 June he was relieved. Major General Thomas Simson Pratt took over, traded speed for Royal Engineer sapping, attacked Huirangi in January 1861 and finally brought about the ceasefire of 18 March. Under them stood Major Thomas Nelson, who led 350 men against Puketakauere; Captain William Messenger, whose column was ambushed after wading a swamp in the dark; Captain Bowdler; Lieutenant Colonel George Freeman Murray, who was censured for his withdrawal at Waireka; Peter Cracroft, captain of HMS Niger, whose bluejackets stormed the pa by night and pulled down the flags; Beauchamp Seymour, commander of the naval brigade; and Charles Brown, the settler captain who held the Jury farmhouse with the armed settlers. On the Maori side Wiremu Kingi was the leader of the resistance, Te Whiti travelled north to seek arbitration, Hapurona was the Te Atiawa war leader who laid out the Puketakauere ambush, Rewi Maniapoto led the night assault on Redoubt No 3, Wiremu Tamihana brokered the truce, and Te Rei Hanataua fell at Waireka. Leading seaman William Odgers of HMS Niger received the Victoria Cross for carrying off the Maori flags, the first such award of the New Zealand Wars.
kits: 卡面這件加特林機槍與塔臘納基戰場無緣：理查德·喬丹·加特林設計的六管機槍一八六〇年做出原型，一八六二年十一月四日取得美國專利，服役期由一八六二年到一九一一年，管數六至十管，操作組四人，科特一八七七年十管型重七十七公斤有奇，.58 口徑每分鐘二百發、.30 口徑可達每分鐘四百至九百發。它第一次上戰場是在美國內戰，一八六四至一八六五年彼得斯堡圍城戰的塹壕裡，由北方聯邦軍的指揮官自掏腰包購買使用；它從未到過紐西蘭。戰場上真正扮演連續壓制角色的，是英軍的二十四磅臼砲與二十四磅火箭：一八六〇年三月十七日在 Te Kohia，兩門臼砲一天之內發射二百發；六月二十七日 Puketakauere 又是兩門臼砲；三月二十八日 Waireka，海軍水兵自約七百米外以火箭齊射後夜襲 pā。步兵主力是 1853 年式恩菲爾德步槍，槍長一點四四米、重四公斤、配五十三厘米插座刺刀，膛線有效射程三百至四百米；民兵手上則是一八四〇年代的老滑膛槍，每人只發三十發子彈。毛利方面裝備雙管霰彈槍、商用步槍與少量來福槍，彈藥靠黑市供應。防禦工事的關鍵是 pā：木柵外編上紐西蘭亞麻的葉片以吸收彈丸，柵欄離地數厘米讓射手從下方開火，留有致命缺口，內挖壕溝與步槍坑，後來再加抗砲掩體，整座堡壘只留一面暴露面引敵來攻。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun on this card never reached the Taranaki battlefield. Richard Jordan Gatling's six-barrel weapon was built as a prototype in 1860, was patented in the United States on 4 November 1862, saw service from 1862 to 1911, had six to ten barrels, needed a crew of four, and the Colt model of 1877 with ten barrels weighed a little over 77 kilograms; it fired 200 rounds a minute in .58 calibre and 400 to 900 rounds a minute in .30 calibre. Its first use in warfare came in the American Civil War, in the trenches of the Siege of Petersburg between 1864 and 1865, where Union commanders bought their own guns out of their own pockets; it never came to New Zealand. What actually played the part of sustained suppressive fire on this battlefield was the British twenty-four-pounder howitzer and the twenty-four-pounder Congreve rocket: on 17 March 1860 at Te Kohia two howitzers fired two hundred rounds in a single day; on 27 June at Puketakauere there were two howitzers again; and on 28 March at Waireka naval bluejackets rocketed the pa from about 700 metres before storming it at night. The infantry backbone was the Pattern 1853 Enfield, 1.44 metres long, 4 kilograms heavy, with a 53-centimetre socket bayonet and a rifled range of 300 to 400 metres; the militia carried old smoothbore muskets of the 1840s, each man issued with only thirty rounds. The Maori equipped themselves with double-barrel shotguns, trade muskets and a few rifles, their ammunition coming from the black market. The key to the defensive works was the pa: a timber palisade faced with woven New Zealand flax leaves to absorb musket balls, the palisade raised a few centimetres off the ground so that muskets could be fired from underneath, gaps left in it that acted as killing traps, with trenches and rifle pits dug inside, and later artillery shelters added, the whole fort presenting a single exposed face to invite attack.
tactics: 兩邊打的都是塹壕對塹壕。英軍一八六〇年的戰術是分縱隊、迂迴、夜間行軍與臼砲火箭齊射：六月二十七日納爾遜把三百五十人分成三路，主力一百八十人帶兩門臼砲由北面逼近，一百二十五人的梅西傑縱隊在冬雨裡摸黑穿過沼澤與蕨叢從東側奪 Puketakauere，六十人的鮑德勒隊佔住北面高地封住退路；結果主隊被壕溝裡的近距離火力打亂，縱隊遭伏擊，多人溺斃在氾濫的惠塔拉河。一八六一年起普拉特改用工兵掘進：自一月二十二日起晝夜挖地道，掘進段長達七百六十八碼，穿過惠朗基的步槍坑，逼使對方放棄前線退回 Pukerangiora，再沿線修六座碉堡，把進逼點一直推到惠塔拉河上方的懸崖。毛利方打得極不對稱：在自己選定的地方設伏，Onukukaitara 掛旗作餌而把真正守軍藏進 Puketakauere 的深壕，天然沖溝兩側的伏兵把英軍縱隊割成兩場戰鬥；同時以戰隊遊擊燒毀 Omata 一帶農莊，斷糧逼和。三月二十八日 Waireka 還示範了另一種打法：英軍指揮官默里吹號撤退，把志願隊與民兵孤立在 Jury 農莊，水兵趁夜以火箭加突擊攻下 Kaipopo pā。停火則由維雷米·塔米哈納在三月十八日斡旋達成。
tacticsEn: Both sides fought a war of trenches against trenches. The British tactics of 1860 were columns, flanking, night movement and combined howitzer and rocket fire: on 27 June Nelson divided 350 men into three, Nelson himself with 180 men and the two howitzers coming down from the north, Messenger with 125 men feeling through a swamp and heavy fern in the winter rain to seize Puketakauere from the east, and Bowdler with 60 men taking a mound between the pa and the camp to block the northern escape. The result was that the main body was thrown into confusion by close-range fire out of the trenches, the flank column was ambushed, and men were drowned in the flooded Waitara River as they fled. From 1861 Pratt changed over to Royal Engineer sapping: from 22 January the engineers dug day and night, the sap ran 768 yards, crossed the rifle pits of Huirangi, forced the Maori to abandon the forward line and fall back on Pukerangiora, and six more redoubts were built as the advance continued, pushing the point of approach up to the cliffs above the Waitara River. The Maori fought very asymmetrically: they chose their own ground, hung a flag over the empty fort of Onukukaitara to make a false target while the real garrison lay deep in the trenches of Puketakauere, and ambushers in the natural gullies cut the British columns into two separate battles; at the same time war parties raided and burned the farms around Omata to cut the food supply and force a peace. Waireka on 28 March showed another pattern: the British commander Murray sounded the retreat, leaving the volunteers and militia isolated at the Jury farmhouse, and bluejackets took advantage of the dark to bombard and storm the Kaipopo pa. The truce was brokered by Wiremu Tamihana on 18 March.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。土地爭議是惠塔拉佩卡佩卡地塊六百英畝，約二點四平方公里，一八五九年十二月先付一百英鎊訂金；一八六〇年二月二十二日宣布戒嚴，二月二十四日簽契，五日四百名英軍登陸惠塔拉築堡，十三日開始測量，十五至十六日維雷米·金吉在 Te Kohia 築起約六百五十平方碼的 L 形 pā，內有十個以木頭與泥土頂蓋的防砲掩體，十七日英軍以近五百人、兩門二十四磅臼砲開火一整天後對方夜間放棄。三月二十八日 Waireka，英軍出動三百三十五人：海軍二十八人、第 65 團八十八人、塔臘納基來福鎗志願隊一百零三人、民兵五十六人，每人配三十發子彈；毛利方在沖溝裏約二百人。英軍傷亡十四人，毛利方陣亡人數各說法在十七至四十之間。Puketakauere 之戰英軍投入三百五十人、兩門臼砲，陣亡三十二人、負傷三十四人，接近參戰兵力的五分之一；毛利方傷亡約五人。六月二十七日之後英軍增援到約二千人；九月普拉特以一千四百人掃蕩惠塔拉上游，十一月六日以一千人擊潰五十至一百五十名王派戰士。一八六〇年十二月二十九至三十一日攻 Kairau，英軍一日耗去步槍彈七萬發、實彈一百二十發，陣亡三人、負傷二十人；一八六一年一月十四日以十一小時築成二號碉堡並駐兵一百二十人，十八日築成三號碉堡、駐兵三百人，一月二十三日凌晨三時半毛利人以一百四十人夜襲三號碉堡，英軍陣亡五人、負傷十一人。全戰英軍與志願民兵共二百三十七人陣亡或負傷，另有約一百二十人病逝於新普利茅斯；毛利方至少九十九人死傷。兵力總量為帝國部隊約三千五百人，毛利方面在數百至一千五百之間浮動，一八六一年一月大王派戰隊加入時峰值約八百人。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The disputed land was the 600-acre, roughly 2.4 square kilometre Pekapeka block at Waitara, on which a 100 pound deposit was paid in December 1859; martial law was proclaimed on 22 February 1860, the deed was executed on 24 February, four hundred British soldiers landed at Waitara and fortified on the 5th, the survey began on the 13th, and on the 15th and 16th Wiremu Kingi built an L-shaped pa of some 650 square yards at Te Kohia, with ten bomb-proof bunkers roofed with timber and earth; on the 17th, with nearly 500 men and two twenty-four-pounder howitzers, the British fired all day and the Maori abandoned the works that night. At Waireka on 28 March the British column numbered 335: 28 naval men, 88 of the 65th Regiment, 103 Taranaki Rifle Volunteers and 56 militia, each man with thirty rounds; about 200 Maori were in the gully. British losses were 14 killed and wounded, and Maori deaths are given anywhere from 17 to 40 depending on the account. At Puketakauere the British committed 350 men and two howitzers and lost 32 killed and 34 wounded, close to one man in five of those engaged; Maori losses were about five. After 27 June British strength in the district was raised to about 2,000; in September Pratt swept the upper Waitara with 1,400 men, and on 6 November a force of 1,000 routed a Kingite war party of 50 to 150. Attacking Kairau on 29 to 31 December 1860, the British expended 70,000 rifle rounds and 120 rounds of shot and shell in a single day and lost three killed and 20 wounded; Redoubt No 2 was built in eleven hours on 14 January 1861 and garrisoned by 120 men, Redoubt No 3 on the 18th by 300 men, and at half past three in the morning of 23 January 140 Maori stormed Redoubt No 3, the British losing five killed and 11 wounded. Over the whole war British regular, volunteer and militia losses were 237 killed or wounded, with about 120 more dying of disease at New Plymouth; at least 99 Maori were killed or wounded. The overall forces were about 3,500 imperial troops against Maori numbers fluctuating between a few hundred and about 1,500, with a peak of roughly 800 in January 1861 when Kingite war parties joined in.
cause: 起因是一塊六百英畝土地的賣法。這塊地叫佩卡佩卡，位置在惠塔拉河口附近，正好可以做北塔臘納基的港口與城鎮，落實後等於打開新普利茅斯到惠塔拉河之間整片土地的買賣先例。一八五七年 Te Āti Awa 的次級首領 Te Teira 主動提出賣地，族群大首領 Wiremu Kīngi 立即否決，理由是土地屬集體所有，Te Teira 無權單獨出售；後來他改口稱自己一家才是唯一業主，只是不想土地受干擾。支持買地的伊哈亞·基里庫馬拉兄弟則在報紙上寫信，說歐洲人進駐可以讓歸國奴隸生活無虞，也少幾次懷卡托戰隊的報復。總督布朗認為毛利人既然可以賣就有權賣，他要在一個人身上立下英王主權高於本地首領的榜樣，於是明知有爭議仍收下這筆交易，並準備用武力落實。更深的背景是一八四〇年《懷唐基條約》翻譯的落差：英方理解為英王取得全部主權，毛利領袖則認為英王只當了全國的總督，土地、村莊仍在自己手裡；一八五〇年代興起的毛利王運動更把反對賣地與反對主權吞併掛鈎。土地之外還有火藥線：一八五八年一月反對賣地的卡塔托雷被殺，同年成立塔臘納基民兵，一八五九年成立志願來福鎗隊，局勢與武力都已備好。三月十五至十六日維雷米·金吉帶八十人築起 Te Kohia 的 pā 卡住路口，十七日英軍在要求投降被拒後開火，戰爭就這樣開始。
causeEn: The cause was the way a block of 600 acres was sold. The land was the Pekapeka block near the mouth of the Waitara River, exactly where a port and township for northern Taranaki were wanted; once it was settled it would have set a precedent for the sale of all the land between New Plymouth and the Waitara River. In 1857 Te Teira, a minor rangatira of Te Atiawa, offered the land to the government and Wiremu Kingi, the paramount chief of the iwi, vetoed it at once on the ground that the land was collectively owned and Te Teira had no right to sell it alone; he later conceded that he and his family were the sole owners but said he simply did not want the land disturbed. Ihaia Kirikumara and his brother Tamati, who supported the sale, wrote to the newspapers claiming that European occupation would allow returned slaves to live in security and lessen the chance that Waikato war parties would return. Governor Browne held that Maori who wished to sell had the right to sell, and he wanted to demonstrate on one man that the sovereignty of the Crown stood above that of a local chief; so he took the transaction over with full knowledge of the dispute and prepared to enforce it by force. Behind this lay a translation gap in the Treaty of Waitangi of 1840: the British read the treaty as the Crown taking sovereignty, while Maori leaders understood that the Queen was only governor of the country, and that the land, the villages and the treasures remained theirs; the Maori King Movement, which grew up in the 1850s, tied opposition to land sales to opposition to annexation. There was a fuse outside the land question as well: Katatore, who opposed selling, was killed in January 1858, the Taranaki Militia was raised that year and the volunteer rifle company in 1859, so that both the grievance and the means of force were ready. On 15 and 16 March Wiremu Kingi and some eighty men built the Te Kohia pa across the road; on the 17th, when the demand to surrender was refused, the British opened fire and the war began.
impact: 這場戰爭在制度與法律上的餘震比戰場上的傷亡更深。一九九六年懷唐基法庭發表《塔臘納基報告：第一份土著索償報告》，認定這場戰爭是政府挑起的，政府是侵略方，其動用武力的做法不正當，並引述一位資深憲法律師的意見，指總督與若干軍官可能需要承擔刑事與民事責任；最高法院法官威廉·西姆的話被後人反覆引用：毛利人被當作叛徒對待，在他們尚未有任何叛亂行為之前，戰爭就已經對他們宣告。一個由殖民政府發起的戰爭，結果由國家的司法機構在三十年後判它不正當，這在紐西蘭史上是沒有先例的。土地與權利的後果更直接：一八六一年停火後雙方都沒有履行協議，爭議地段的合法性懸而未決，一八六三年政府以叛亂為名大舉沒收約一萬二千平方公里毛利土地，約佔紐西蘭全國土地面積百分之四；同年爆發入侵懷卡托的戰役，隨後是一八六四至一八六六年的第二次塔臘納基戰爭、一八六八至一八六九年蒂托科瓦魯戰爭，直到一八八一年帕里哈卡被武力清剿，毛利王運動才真正走到盡頭。毛利方面的收穫不在土地而在政治：這場戰爭證明土地買賣可以引動全北島的部族聯盟，王運動因此獲得聲望與信仰上的合法性，一八六一年七月三日 Wiriwiri 大會上千人宣示支持，一八六二年七月 Kapoaiaia 大會六百人宣告 Waireka 以南一帶仍是毛利地，並警告任何試圖修通道路的舉動都等同宣戰。英國方面則付出制度成本：帝國軍在紐西蘭的駐扎規模一度膨脹到一萬人，倫敦批評高昂的駐軍費用，殖民地政府被迫改行自力政策，帝國軍於一八六六至一八六七年陸續撤回本土，最後一個團更拖到一八七〇年才走。戰場本身也留了下來：Te Kohia 的 pā 遺址二〇一六年由新普利茅斯區議會以七十一萬五千紐元買回，與 Puke Ariki 博物館一起做保育；惠塔拉河畔的塹壕與碉堡線，則是英國軍隊在紐西蘭所建規模最大的野戰工事之一。
impactEn: The institutional and legal aftershock of this war ran deeper than the casualties on the field. In 1996 the Waitangi Tribunal issued the Taranaki Report: Kaupapa Tuatahi, finding that the war was begun by the Government, that the Government was the aggressor and that its resort to armed force was unlawful, and quoting an opinion obtained from a senior constitutional lawyer to the effect that the Governor and certain officers might be liable to criminal and civil charges; the words of the Supreme Court judge Sir William Sim have been quoted ever since, that the Natives were treated as rebels and war declared against them before they had engaged in rebellion of any kind, and that in their eyes the fight was not against the Queen's sovereignty but a struggle for house and home. A war started by the colonial government and pronounced unlawful by the country's own courts three decades later had no precedent in New Zealand history. The consequences for land and rights were even more direct: after the 1861 truce neither side fulfilled the agreement, the legality of the disputed block stayed unresolved, and in 1863 the government confiscated about 12,000 square kilometres of Maori land, roughly four per cent of the country's area, on the ground of rebellion; the invasion of the Waikato followed in the same year, then the Second Taranaki War of 1864 to 1866 and Titokowaru's War of 1868 to 1869, and the Maori King Movement did not come to an end until Parihaka was cleared by force in 1881. What the Maori gained was not land but political capital: the war showed that a land sale could mobilise iwi right across the North Island, and the King Movement drew from it standing and religious legitimacy, with a thousand people pledging support at the hui at Wiriwiri on 3 July 1861 and six hundred declaring the land south of Waireka still theirs at Kapoaiaia in July 1862, warning that any attempt to push a road through it would be an act of war. The British paid in institutional terms: the imperial garrison in New Zealand swelled to about 10,000 men, London complained about the cost, the colonial government was pushed into a policy of self-reliance, and imperial troops were withdrawn from the country in 1866 and 1867, the last regiment not leaving until 1870. The battlefield itself survives as well: the site of the Te Kohia pa was bought back by the New Plymouth District Council in 2016 for NZ$715,000 and conserved with the Puke Ariki museum, and the line of saps and redoubts above the Waitara River remains one of the most extensive field works ever built by British troops in New Zealand.
result: 結果是一場沒有勝負的停火。一八六一年三月十八日，在維雷米·塔米哈納斡旋下雙方達成停火，兩邊都沒有明確接受對方的條件；英軍靠工兵掘進修到惠朗基與 Kairau 一線，壓住了 Te Arei 防線，卻沒能攻下 Pukerangiora，毛利人守住了村莊，卻沒有拿回惠塔拉的法定權益。戰術上英軍自一八六一年起改用短管卡賓槍，林地機動性明顯改善；政治上雙方都把問題留到下一次：土地買賣的合法性始終沒有一個雙方都簽字的結論，停火協議的條款也無人履行。戰事因此一路拖長，一八六三年政府藉口沒收土地，一八六三至一八六四年入侵懷卡托，一八六四年起第二次塔臘納基戰爭，一八六八年的蒂托科瓦魯戰爭，直到一八七二年人員傷亡與土地沒收都告一段落。對卡面這件加特林機槍而言，這場戰爭還有一層反諷：它同年問世、兩年後拿到專利、數年後才第一次上戰場，卻與塔臘納基毫無關係；真正決定戰局的新技術是工兵的地道與碉堡線，而最後收場的不是武器，是一紙由第三方促成、雙方都不認輸的停火。
resultEn: The result was a ceasefire that neither side could call a win. On 18 March 1861 a truce was arranged through the mediation of Wiremu Tamihana, and neither side explicitly accepted the terms of the other; the British had pushed their saps and redoubts as far as the Huirangi and Kairau line and pinned down the Te Arei defences, but they did not take Pukerangiora, and the Maori kept their villages without recovering their legal title at Waitara. Tactically the British turned to short carbines from 1861 and their mobility in the bush improved markedly; politically both sides left the problem for another day, because the legality of the sale never got a conclusion signed by both parties and the clauses of the truce were never implemented. The war therefore ran on: the land confiscations of 1863, the invasion of the Waikato in 1863 and 1864, the Second Taranaki War from 1864, Titokowaru's War in 1868, and it was not until 1872 that the loss of life and the confiscation of land had run their course. For the Gatling gun on this card there is an irony in all of it. It appeared in the same year, took out its patent two years later, saw its first combat a few years after that, and had nothing whatever to do with Taranaki; the new technique that actually decided the fighting was the sappers' sap and the line of redoubts, and what closed the business at the end was not a weapon but a piece of paper agreed by a third party, with neither side conceding defeat.
